# Scale benchmark (chunked profiling + DuckDB)

<!-- Generated by benchmarks/scale_benchmark.py - do not edit by hand; re-run the script. -->

Every number on this page was measured by `services/engine/benchmarks/scale_benchmark.py` in the run described below.
Nothing here is typed in by hand. Wall time, memory and date are measurements and change from run to run; the generated data and the profile do not.

## Headline

- **Rows:** 1,000,000 x 10 columns (74.1 MB of CSV)
- **Wall time:** 21.46 s (46,592 rows/s)
- **Peak memory:** 510 MB resident (maxrss), of which 243 MB is the interpreter + libraries before profiling starts
- **Chunk size:** 100,000 rows (10 chunks)
- **Health Score of the generated file:** 96

## Runs

| Run | Rows | Columns | CSV size (MB) | Chunks | Wall time (s) | Rows/s | Peak memory (MB) | Baseline before profiling (MB) |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| headline | 1,000,000 | 10 | 74.1 | 10 | 21.46 | 46,592 | 510 | 243 |
| smaller file, same code | 250,000 | 10 | 18.5 | 3 | 5.42 | 46,108 | 325 | 237 |

Peak memory is the profiling process's `resource.getrusage` maxrss high-water mark, measured in a fresh child process so the data generator cannot inflate it; it includes DuckDB's native memory. Wall time covers `profile_file` only (no imports, no generation).

Going from 250,000 to 1,000,000 rows (4.0x the data) changed peak memory by +185 MB (1.57x). Memory is therefore bounded but not flat: the pandas pass holds one chunk whatever the file size, while DuckDB's exact distinct and duplicate-row hash tables grow with column cardinality (`order_id` is unique in every row). DuckDB is given a memory limit (1 GB by default) and a spill directory.

## Setup

- **Date (UTC):** 2026-11-13
- **Platform:** Linux-7.0.0-44-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39, Python 3.12.3, 4 logical CPUs, 7.7 GB RAM; pandas 2.1.4, numpy 1.26.4, duckdb 2.0.0
- **Seed:** 42 (`numpy.random.default_rng`), so the generated CSV is identical on every run.
- **Generated data:** 1% of rows are exact duplicates of the first rows (appended last), ~10% of `discount` and ~5% of `note` are blank, `customer` has ~200k distinct values, `order_id` is unique. Written to a temp directory and deleted after the run; nothing is committed.
- **Path under test:** `app.engine.scale.profile_file` with chunk size 100,000: a pandas `chunksize` pass (row count, nulls, numeric min/max) then DuckDB over the CSV for exact distinct counts, sums, medians, duplicate rows and top values, then the same `profile.health_score` the in-memory path uses.
- **Not measured here:** the in-memory path (`profile_dataframe`), which refuses files over 50,000 rows / 10 MB.

## Correctness checks (against planted truth)

| Check | Headline run | Smaller run |
|:--|:--|:--|
| row count equals rows written | pass | pass |
| duplicate_rows equals planted duplicates | pass | pass |
| column count | pass | pass |

Column types inferred for the headline file: `order_id` id, `customer` text, `region` categorical, `status` categorical, `amount` numeric, `quantity` numeric, `discount` numeric, `is_member` boolean, `placed_on` datetime, `note` text.
